background_notes.fact: For the Z-module M and field K regarded as a Z-module, any biadditive Z-balanced map M×K→A induces a unique additive map M⊗_Z K→A. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors. Thus the balanced swaps m⊗α↦α⊗m and α⊗m↦m⊗α are mutually inverse K-linear maps for the actions on the K factors; identities between additive maps may be checked on pure tensors.

Both swaps are biadditive and their Z-balance relations are explicitly checked.

background_notes.justification: The tensor product is the quotient of the free abelian group on pairs by the biadditivity and balance relations; a map respecting these relations descends uniquely, and pure tensors generate the quotient. On a pure tensor, the swaps commute with multiplication by β∈K because α becomes βα on either side, and the two composites return the original tensor. Additivity extends these calculations to all tensors.

background_notes.fact: If s:U→T and t:T→U are inverse K-linear maps and T has a finite basis of n elements, then applying t to that basis yields a basis of U of n elements. In particular, dim U=dim T=n, finite-dimensionality transfers, and T≠0 implies U≠0.
